name: Adaptify SEO One-Click Publishing
author: hansjan

sections.description:
Adaptify SEO One-Click Publishing connects your WordPress site to Adaptify’s external content publishing service. It lets scheduled articles prepared in Adaptify be published to your WordPress site through the WordPress REST API.

After activation, a WordPress administrator must explicitly connect the site from the plugin settings page. Adaptify shows a connection code for the site; the administrator pastes that code into the plugin settings and clicks Connect to Adaptify. WordPress then creates a native Application Password for that administrator account and the plugin sends the site URL, WordPress username, generated Application Password, and Adaptify connection code to Adaptify’s API endpoint at https://api.ttsp4712.ai/add-wp-pw over HTTPS so Adaptify can publish scheduled content through the WordPress REST API. No Application Password is created or sent during plugin activation. The Application Password can be managed from the user’s WordPress profile or the plugin settings page.

External service:

  • Service: Adaptify
  • Website: https://adaptify.ai/
  • API endpoint: https://api.ttsp4712.ai/
  • Terms: https://adaptify.ai/terms
  • Privacy policy: https://adaptify.ai/privacy-policy
  • Purpose: scheduled publishing, publishing status callbacks, plugin lifecycle event logging, plugin status checks, and SEO metadata synchronization.
  • Data sent during plugin status checks and metadata synchronization: site URL, plugin version, WordPress version, publishing status, PHP version, permalink structure, multisite status, home URL, and homepage verification tag sync requests.
  • Data sent during plugin activation and deactivation events: site URL, event type, plugin version, and WordPress version.
  • Data sent during publishing status callbacks: site URL, article ID, keyword ID, WordPress post ID, post URL, publishing status, and error message when publishing fails.
  • Data sent after explicit administrator connection: site URL, WordPress username, generated WordPress Application Password, and Adaptify connection code.
  • Data received: scheduled article content and SEO metadata to publish on the connected WordPress site.
sections.changelog:
1.5.14

  • Support updating an existing post when Adaptify republishes an article through the plugin fallback (previously the fallback could only create new posts). Reports the plugin version so the backend only sends updates to plugins that support them.
  • Tested and verified compatible with WordPress 7.1.

1.5.13

  • Update the public plugin display name to Adaptify SEO One-Click Publishing for WordPress.org review.

1.5.12

  • Restrict the diagnostic REST endpoint to authorized administrators.
  • Move settings page styles into an enqueued admin stylesheet.
  • Prefix plugin globals, functions, classes, hooks, and cache keys more consistently.
  • Update WordPress compatibility metadata and readme fields for WordPress.org review.
  • Replace direct debug logging and tighten output escaping for verification meta tags.

1.5.11

  • Require an explicit Connect to Adaptify action before creating and sending a WordPress Application Password.
  • Require the Adaptify connection code so the connection can be attached directly to the right Adaptify site.
  • Clarify the connection disclosure in the plugin settings page and clean up only Adaptify-created application passwords.

1.5.10

  • Clarify the Adaptify external service connection, WordPress Application Password creation, credential handoff, and revocation options in the settings page and readme.
  • Update plugin metadata to mark compatibility through WordPress 7.0.

1.5.9

  • Category fallback: match custom category instructions locally when REST API is blocked by security plugins
  • Supports quoted names (straight and curly) and bare short category names
  • Looks up existing categories locally and falls back to the site default if no match is found

1.5.8

  • Generalized homepage verification tags to support full HTML snippets and multiple meta tags
  • Plugin now consumes tags_html payload and safely renders all returned verification tags
